$comment: Ground truth established by reading each repository directly — counting the
directories the project itself uses to organise its components — WITHOUT
running Lyse. This is the number a design-system engineer would give if asked
'how many components does this library ship?'. It is the only thing in the
repo that Lyse's own output was not used to produce, which is what makes it
an oracle rather than a snapshot.
`heldOut: true` means the repo is NOT in .bench-corpus, so it took no part in
rule calibration. Regressions caught on a held-out repo are real; regressions
caught on an in-corpus repo may be train-on-test artefacts.
Tolerance is deliberately loose. A design system's component count is not a
single well-defined integer (sub-components, compound exports, internal
primitives), so this harness answers 'is Lyse in the right order of
magnitude, and did that change?' — not 'is Lyse exactly right'. Zero where
there should be hundreds is the failure mode it exists to catch.

repos.name: bad-app
repos.componentsDir: (none — a CRA tutorial app styled with Bootstrap classes)

tolerance.$comment: A reported count is accepted when it lands within [components / factorLow, components * factorHigh]. Over-counting is the more forgivable direction: a design system legitimately exposes sub-components the canonical directory listing does not.
